name: Gotland Pony
notes: The Gotlandsruss, or just the Russ - the island landrace of Gotland in the Baltic. Older names are better: Skogruss, the little horse of the woods, and Skogsbaggar, forest rams.

Dun is the signature family and sits near three-quarters of founders, over a bay-led base, so bay dun leads with grullo and red dun behind it. d1 is carried on purpose - primitive marking without body dilution, which is what a landrace should look like.

Single cream is deliberately present and double cream deliberately impossible: the Swedish conservation description excludes homozygous cream, not cream itself, so Cr/N ships and Cr/Cr does not. A founder will never be cremello, though breeding two carriers still can be.
Grey and tobiano are excluded by the same conservation profile and are forced wild outright, not merely kept rare.

No gait locus, and for once that is measured rather than assumed: a published sample of 28 Gotland ponies found the DMRT3 gait-keeper allele at zero frequency. The breed's sporting reputation is pony trotting, which is a trot.

Champagne, silver, mushroom, pearl, roan, rabicano, leopard and every white-pattern locus are forced wild - no breed-specific evidence for any. Flaxen is the one cautious aesthetic addition and is not a documented population estimate.
Cold tolerant partially: wind-exposed Baltic country - mixed forest, heath, thin soils and cold wet winters rather than lush pasture - and a managed semi-feral herd still lives out at Lojsta Hed.

It came within a hair of ending. By 1922 the core remnant was seven mares, one young stallion and six young horses; Welsh and Welsh Mountain stallions were brought in in 1951 and 1957 against the inbreeding and their lines run through the modern population, with no outside introductions since.
Uncommon rather than rare on the numbers: NordGen recorded about 2,500 mares in Sweden in 2020 and conservation sources put the world population at roughly 6,000 to 8,000.
All disorders clear. Importing Arabian, Quarter Horse, Friesian or warmblood rates into a small Swedish pony population would be inventing them.
The famously hard sound hooves, the pony-trotting talent and the long back are none of them modelled.
